title: Oven-Roasted Smoky Mexican Ikura Birria
description: A velvety, brunch‑ready Mexican birria wrapped in puff pastry and crowned with salmon roe, bursting with smoky flavors and sugar‑free goodness.
instructions: Toast the ancho and guajillo chilies, remove stems, roughly chop, and blend with onion, garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, oregano, and a splash of beef broth to form a smooth sauce.
In a heavy skillet, heat olive oil over medium‑high, brown the beef cubes on all sides, then transfer them to a baking dish.
Pour the chili sauce over the beef, add the remaining broth and soy sauce, cover with foil, and bake in the preheated oven for 2 hours until the meat is tender.
Remove the beef, shred it with two forks, stir it back into the sauce, and let it simmer uncovered for 20 minutes to thicken.
While the sauce simmers, roll out the puff pastry to 12x12 inches, place shredded birria in the center, drizzle with a little extra sauce, and top with a generous spoonful of ikura.
Fold the pastry edges over the filling, seal with a fork, brush the top with beaten egg, and bake at 200C for 15 minutes until golden.
Let the pastry cool for 5 minutes, slice into squares, and serve warm with lime wedges.
